w: On 14 December 1965, in Gondal, the Crown Prince of Bhavnagar, Shri Virbhadrasinhji, was coming to the Akshar Mandir for darshan. Yogiji Maharaj had all the preparations made for his welcome. Good seats were arranged for him in the assembly hall. Instead of sitting on the seat where he usually sat, Swamishri sat down below on a cushion. When everyone pressed him greatly to sit up on his seat, he pleaded, "No, please let me sit down here." After everyone insisted a great deal, Swamishri reluctantly sat on the seat.

Just then the Crown Prince arrived with his family and with leaders such as Kiritsinh and Mohanbhai Rathod. Collector Chudasama Saheb and Bhagvatsinhji welcomed everyone. After darshan at the Akshar Deri and in the mandir, everyone came to Swamishri in the assembly hall. Getting down from his seat and going forward, Swamishri welcomed the Crown Prince with garlands. Swamishri gave everyone his gracious blessings. The Crown Prince too, feeling fulfilled at receiving Yogiji Maharaj's humility and blessings, humbly bowed at his feet. After the formalities, everyone went to take prasad.

After that, all the devotees were bowing to Swamishri one by one. Just then an elderly man dressed in court attire bowed to Swamishri and stood at a distance. Swamishri's eyes fell on him. He lovingly called him over and, blessing him, asked in a voice full of affection, "Who are you?"
"I am the Crown Prince's driver," the old man replied with folded hands.
"Is that so, Driver Saheb?" said Swamishri, and once again gave him a pat of blessing.

"What a difference between the Crown Prince and me... and yet the blessings of such a great sadhu... just like Bapu, he welcomed and blessed me too... the same love... indeed even more..." Experiencing this shower of nectar from Swamishri, the driver felt utterly fulfilled. As if that were not enough, Swamishri called him close and gave him prasad with his own hands. The driver, who had come with an empty heart, left with a full heart.

jc.t: Murti pratishtha in the Kolkata mandir; 52nd birthday festival in the evening, during the train yatra

w: Swamishri blessed 65 students of the BAPS hostel for tribal boys in Ukai.

A devotee from Chicago came to Swamishri with his young son, Jay, who was celebrating his sixth birthday today. Jay respecfully offered panchang pranam to Swamishri and said, "Bapa, today is my birthday." Swamishri smiled at him and affectionately placed his hand on Jay's head to bless him. Jay's father asked him, "What present are going to give to Swamibapa to mark your birthday today?" Excitedly, Jay replied, "Bapa! from today I will not watch TV." Swamishri was extremely delighted to hear Jay's commitment and blessed him again, saying, "That good. It is a great commitment. Maharaj will be pleased. Yogiji Maharaj will also be pleased. It will bring you much wisdom and you will be able to offer worship to God."

On the occasion of the 31st patotsav (inauguration anniversary) of the Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, a mahapuja was performed. Three-hundred devotees and wellwishers participated in the puja. Swamishri performed pujan and arti of Thakorji. A beautiful annakut of 600 items had been prepared by the local women's wing!

During late afternoon Swamishri departed from Mahelav and arrived in Piplata to perform pujan and arti of the murtis. After blessing the devotees Swamishri left at 5.45 pm and arrived at Amdavad mandir at 6.35 pm.

st.t: The Shining Stars of BAPS Children, INDIA
w: T hese days, such great and noble values being in such small children is a true miracle. Bal mandal, however, is a source of countless such miracles.

Here, young balaks are inspired to be like Dhruv, Nachiketa, Prahlad, Bharat and Eklavya. Here, balaks are taught the knowledge of atma and Paramatma from a very young age. Here, the fires of self confidence and determination are lit within children. As a result, BAPS children have developed extraordinary talents and have succeeded in countless fields. Nine such balaks with exceptional achievements were honored in sabha. Swamishri blessed each of these balaks.

Three years ago, these two balaks, ages 11 and 12, broke a national record by swimming from Dharmatar to the Gateway of India, a 35-kilometer distance. Countless newspapers, magazines and television news channels noted their extraordinary achievement.
Despite living outside of India, this 13-year-old balak has worked hard to please Swamishri by learning Gujarati and passing all satang Exams at a very young age.
From amongst 31 countries and 3,700 children, this 12-year-old balak won 3rd place and 1st place in India in UCMAC's competition involving the ABACUS math technique.
In just three years, this balak has read 20,000 pages of satsang books. Aside from satsang books, he also achieves well in school. He has scored more than 95% in each school standard until now.

Musician. Dancer. Artist of more than 300 masterful paintings and drawings. An expert artist, he has received countless certificates, medals and honors. Moreover, his paintings have been sent to Japan and Korea for display in museums.

An extraordinarily intelligent child, this balak has memorized 425 shlokas and sakhis and 500 Swamini Vato. He has read more than 1200 different books and can speak on the Mahabharat for an astounding six hours.

The evening satsang assembly began with a concert of bhajans by sadhus. Thereafter, Swamishri was honoured with garlands. Finally in his blessings Swamishri inspired, “If you think, you will come to realize that ordinary people, and even kings and millionaires have all passed away. Despite knowing this, we never think and feel that we too are going to die and leave everything behind. It is because of ignorance that we become infatuated and attached. What is ignorance? The belief that ‘I am the body.’ Everyone’s body dies, likewise ours too will die.”
Improving one’s nature

1 December 2008, Tithal A devotee was prone to frequent bouts of depression. As a result, he was given the pink slip at work. In addition, he had daily spats at home. On top of this his daughter got divorced. These social tragedies multiplied his depression manifold. His relatives brought him for Swamishri’s blessings. After listening to the problem Swamishri advised, “Have patience. Nothing good comes out of having tension. You have the refuge of God, a holy Sadhu and satsang. Your satsang , too, is not ordinary. So live in accordance to God’s wishes. You should not quarrel because of your base nature ( swabhav ). Empty your mind of other thoughts, and believe that whatever has happened is due to God’s wish. Decide here and now that you don’t want to get angry and quarrel any more. Say ‘Swaminarayan’ and do mala .” A relative said, “He has become distraught after his daughter’s divorce.” Swamishri added, “Believe it to be God’s wish. Believe it to be due to her past karmas. It must be her fate to experience such pain and suffering. The main problem is that because of your nature others’ minds become agitated, so you should understand and resolve it. If you mend yourself, your daughter will get an appropriate partner.”
Overcoming fear

1 December 2008, , Tithal A spiritually-inclined person narrated his apprehensions to Swamishri, “I just can’t understand why I am always fearful. I keep feeling that I will die this very moment! On coming here to Tithal when I saw the ocean, I worried about what will happen to me!” Swamishri pacified him with soothing words, “God is with you, so there is no need to fear. By being fearful one cannot accomplish anything. Engage yourself in daily effort and remember God. Nothing is going to happen to you.”
God always does good for all

4 December 2008, , Tithal A God-loving person expressed his problem through a fax addressed to Swamishri. He questioned as to where God was, “I applied twice for my visas. I feel that despite doing satsang God doesn’t give me success in my work. And for those who don’t do satsang and don’t believe in God, their work is done.” Swamishri blessed him, “When your mundane wish is not fulfilled then understand it to be for your good. Sometimes God tests us. God always does what is best and will do so. Try again for the third time. Remember God and his glory when you go to the visa office. God will do good for you.”
Key to god’s presence

16 December 2008, , Navsari Nainesh, a satsangi youth of London, rang up Swamishri and said, “Financially, times are bad and critical for us here. You too are not coming here, so there is a bad time (crisis) for us in all aspects. Swamishri replied, “God and his devotees never have ‘bad’ times. There are ups and downs in our world. During such times one must be patient and do bhajan.” Nainesh added, “Your darshan here would bring joy to us.” Swamishri advised, “Understand first that we are together. Learning and imbibing this spiritual knowledge will make you happy and joyous. Whenever you remember, while doing puja or visiting the mandir, God and his Sadhu are with you.”Swamishri underlined to all pious seekers to foster spiritual understanding and consciousness.

After the morning puja, during the meal, there was talk about comforts and discomforts. There was also talk about what comforts the sadhus have now by Pramukh Swami Maharaj's grace. Yagneshwar Swami had come to Mumbai today; as no car came from the mandir to fetch him, he had to come by taxi.
In this context Swamishri, in a light mood, said to him, "You didn't feel bad, did you?"
Adarshjivan Swami said, "You have lived in such a way that there is no question of anyone feeling bad in any situation. You too have travelled like this, in bullock carts and on foot."
Swamishri said, "Where are we compared to them? What hardships our gurus endured compared to us! We have a little discomfort now and then, but they worked only amid discomforts."
Gnanvatsal Swami said, "In those days they had no facilities at all, and you had facilities, yet you put up with discomforts and endured."
Adarshjivan Swami said, "At that time their travel was limited too, but you have travelled all over the world enduring discomforts."
Swamishri said, "Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj too travelled all over the world, carrying bundles on their heads."

Adarshjivan Swami said, "Even if someone has a problem with food, they can find the answer from your life; and with vehicles too, there is no problem about comfort or discomfort. In no situation is there anything to feel hurt about. The answer to every question is found in your life itself."
As if he had not heard any of this, Swamishri remained absorbed in singing the praises of his gurus.

Finally he said, "That is what we have to learn. As the great ones did, so we should behave. How many difficulties there were in the time of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj! Travelling in bullock carts, going on foot, and on arriving, cooking for themselves, and cooking for the devotees too, yet they pleased everyone; we should behave the same way."

ds.t: Print Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj
w: Gnanpurush Swami and Adarshmuni Swami, who are travelling in Australia and the Asia Pacific region, came today. They came with the organisation's English publications to have them sanctified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Swamishri turned two or three pages of the book two or three times; on the front page were Maharaj and Swami and on the back page was Swamishri's photo and introduction. In this context Swamishri said, "There should be a photo of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, shouldn't there!" Saying this, he himself began to show: "Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj should be printed beside or behind Akshar Purushottam Maharaj; now all that has been left out. How will the children abroad know who Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj were?"
Swamishri has made this remark many times.
Then, as talk went on, Ruda Swami said, "I have found the biggest mine of wealth: you."
Swamishri at once said, laughing, "Brother, we are plain and dry."
Adarshmuni Swami said, "Lakshmi is said to be the servant of the Sant, isn't she!"
Swamishri said, "That is a matter of glory. We are to do katha, talks and bhajan so that satsang and conviction become firm in the devotees, and through that seva is done."
Gnaneshwar Swami said, "Please cast your glance."
Swamishri said, "If one works hard, the glance follows."

An example of how the transformation of one soul benefits the whole of society is Arvindbhai Patel of Vadodara. When he was not in contact with satsang, his whole life was spent in addictions and many kinds of vices. As a result, at the end of each day the total came to zero, and on top of that there were quarrels and conflict. That same Arvindbhai came into satsang, and such values took root that after that he freed hundreds of young men from the grip of alcohol and addictions. After that he gradually progressed in politics too. He was elected to the post of Deputy Mayor of Vadodara city. Today he phoned.

Blessing him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "You have received the seva of Vadodara city, so my blessings are that good service is done through you. It is through the power of your coming into satsang that this good position has come, so do good work. My blessings are that the city develops and the people are served."
